python_catalog.description: List comprehensions like `[x for x in range(10)]` are a concise way to create lists in Python. However, we can achieve better memory efficiency by using generator expressions like `(x for x in range(10))` instead. List comprehensions create the entire list in memory, while generator expressions generate each element one at a time. We can make the change by replacing the square brackets with parentheses.
